title: One-Syllable Clue · Together
hook: Find a game, gather your friends and start playing.

knows: The group wants an activity to play together.
doesNotKnow: The setup, turn and ending for this house-rule format.

misconception: The group has to know a complicated rulebook before starting.
objective: Learn how to play One-Syllable Clue · Together with friends.

claims.text: Original house rules: Write familiar objects on slips. The lead describes the chosen object using only one-syllable words without saying its name. The group identifies the object and the clue follows the word rule. Play eight turns in total, rotating the lead. The group wins together if at least five turns succeed.
claims.source: Original playable house-rule proposal; not an authoritative ruleset for a traditional game.

claims.text: For this version: 2–8 players; materials: Paper and pencil.
claims.source: Proposed setup and player range for this activity.

recall.question: In One-Syllable Clue, what counts as a successful turn?
options: The lead skips the turn without attempting it.
The group ends the round before anyone plays.
The group identifies the object and the clue follows the word rule.
recall.why: The group identifies the object and the clue follows the word rule.
